title: Retrieval over 46 skill documents, four retrievers, 20 labelled questions
prescribes: Chunk on structure with overlap, embed, retrieve with both lexical and dense signals, fuse and rerank, and evaluate retrieval against labelled queries instead of eyeballing it.
applied: Chunked every installed SKILL.md into 420 passages, indexed them with BM25 and MiniLM-L6 embeddings, fused with reciprocal rank fusion, reranked the top 20 with a cross-encoder, and scored all four against 20 hand-labelled questions.
narrative: The corpus is 420 chunks from 46 documents, averaging 48 words with a 40-word overlap and a split on markdown headings first. Structure-aware chunking matters here because a skill document is a sequence of self-contained instructions -- cutting mid-section produces passages that answer nothing.

Every retriever is scored on the same 20 questions with a known correct skill, so the comparison is a number rather than an impression. BM25 gets recall@1 of 55%, dense embeddings 80%, RRF fusion 85%, and adding the cross-encoder reranker 85%.

The two signals fail differently, which is why fusing helps: BM25 puts the right skill in the top three on 100% of questions but only first on 55% -- it finds the neighbourhood and misranks inside it -- while the dense index ranks better at position one and occasionally misses the neighbourhood entirely. Reciprocal rank fusion takes the better half of each.

The cross-encoder reranker did not help here: recall@1 stays at 85% and MRR moves -0.008, for 606 ms of extra latency per query. That is a real negative result worth keeping: the chunks here average 48 words, and an MS MARCO-trained reranker has little to work with on passages that short. On longer, noisier documents the same step usually earns its cost -- which is the argument for measuring it rather than assuming it.

Cost is asymmetric and worth stating: BM25 answers all 20 queries in 9 ms, the dense search in 3 ms after a 3.8s indexing pass, and the reranking pass costs 12.1s in total because it runs a transformer over 20 query-passage pairs per question. On CPU that dominates the latency budget.

takeaway: Fusing lexical and dense retrieval lifts recall@1 from 55% to 85%, while the cross-encoder rerank adds 606 ms per query and no accuracy on this corpus -- a conclusion only the labelled query set could support.
